content:
SLIDE 1 (Hook):
Trying to pick the "safe" major is the most dangerous career move you can make.

SLIDE 2:
Paul Graham said it plainly: predicting which fields will be valuable is too uncertain to get right. Stop optimizing for a future nobody can see.

SLIDE 3:
The founders who built generational companies weren't chasing trends. They were obsessed with a problem long before the market validated it.

SLIDE 4:
Passion is a leading indicator. Credentials are a lagging one. You hire the person who can't stop thinking about the problem — not the one who optimized their resume for it.

SLIDE 5:
This is how I recruit early team members. I don't care what's on the degree. I care what they build at 2am when nobody's watching.

SLIDE 6:
The irony: the people trying to future-proof their skills are the ones most likely to be disrupted. Obsession compounds. Trend-chasing doesn't.

SLIDE 7:
Your unfair advantage isn't the field you picked. It's the depth you go when everyone else stops.

LAST SLIDE (CTA):
What were you obsessed with before you knew it was "valuable"? That's probably still the answer. Drop it below.
source_story_title: Paul Graham: Focus on Passion, Not Future-Proofing, When Choosing What to Study
source_story_summary: Paul Graham posted his most-engaged advice of the day, urging college students not to try predicting which fields will be valuable in the future — an exercise he considers too uncertain to get right — but instead to pursue whatever they personally find most exciting. The post generated outsized engagement relative to his other tweets, suggesting it struck a broad chord beyond just the startup community.

content:
SLIDE 1 (Hook):
Every time Microsoft holds Build, a category of startups quietly dies. Watch what Satya teases this week very carefully.

SLIDE 2:
Build isn't a conference. It's Microsoft's annual announcement of what they're about to commoditize at the platform layer.

SLIDE 3:
They have deep OpenAI integration, Azure scale, and Copilot embedded across every enterprise touchpoint. That's not a product suite — that's a moat being built in public.

SLIDE 4:
The founders who win aren't the ones ignoring this. They're the ones who read the announcement and immediately ask: "What's now table stakes — and where does the white space open up?"

SLIDE 5:
Every major Azure or Copilot expansion at Build signals where Microsoft is going deep. That's your map for where NOT to compete — and where to build on top.

SLIDE 6:
The smartest play for indie builders and operators: position your product as the layer Microsoft won't build. The specialized, vertical, or last-mile solution their platform will always need.

SLIDE 7:
San Francisco. Satya on stage. Major AI developer platform news incoming. The developer tooling agenda for the next 12 months is about to get written.

LAST SLIDE (CTA):
Are you watching Build to stay informed — or to find your next move? Those are two very different postures. Drop your prediction below: what does Microsoft announce, and who gets disrupted?
source_story_title: Microsoft Build Conference Coming to San Francisco — Satya Nadella Teases Announcement
source_story_summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella posted a countdown to a new Build developer conference in San Francisco, sharing a teaser link and media asset. Build is Microsoft's flagship developer event and typically serves as the venue for major announcements around Azure, AI, Windows, and developer tooling.
